subject.description: Meadows Housekeeping work update for July 19, 2026: inventory processing, reusable product and SDS views, and stable Apps Script navigation.

narrative.promptingSituation: The inventory project still consisted partly of spreadsheet records and experimental pages. Inventory requests needed safe processing, and navigation became unstable when Apps Script pages were embedded.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: The application needed a transactional core that rejected invalid requests without partial effects, plus reusable routed views that could combine product, inventory, and SDS information.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Create a functioning inventory application with validated quantity changes, permanent history, stable navigation, and reusable live-data views.
narrative.approach: Implement the five inventory actions, validate all source and destination conditions before mutation, create accepted event records, build a route map and reusable product template, then replace relative embedded navigation with a shared server-provided appUrl.

progression.description: Implemented Received, Used Up, Removed, Moved, and Count Corrected actions.
progression.result: Accepted requests update quantities and create permanent inventory events.

problemsEncountered.problem: Relative links behaved inconsistently inside embedded Apps Script pages.
problemsEncountered.effect: Links could fail, disappear, or replace the wrong frame.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Used complete appUrl links supplied by the server and routed each request through doGet(e).

problemsEncountered.problem: Invalid inventory operations could risk partial quantity changes or false event records.
problemsEncountered.effect: Inventory history and current quantities could become inaccurate.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Validated the full request before applying changes and excluded rejected requests from Inventory Events.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Use relative links such as ?view=inventory inside embedded pages.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: Relative navigation was simple and worked when the app was opened directly.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: The browser could resolve the wrong frame or base URL in the embedded environment.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Routing and navigation are separate concerns; embedded Apps Script links need a stable complete base URL.

turningPoints.title: Validation became transactional
turningPoints.description: The system was required to reject invalid operations before any quantity or event mutation.

turningPoints.title: Shared appUrl replaced relative navigation

turningPoints.effectOnDirection: The routed interface became stable across all existing views.

keyDecisions.decision: Keep rejected requests visible but out of accepted Inventory Events.
keyDecisions.reason: Failures should remain diagnosable without becoming operational history.
consequences: The system preserves troubleshooting evidence while protecting inventory history.

keyDecisions.decision: Use one reusable Product View template.
keyDecisions.reason: Product pages share structure and differ mainly by product ID.
alternativesConsidered: Create a separate HTML file for each product
consequences: Product detail pages became easier to maintain and extend.

keyDecisions.decision: Provide a complete appUrl from the server.
keyDecisions.reason: Relative paths were unreliable in embedded Apps Script contexts.
consequences: All navigation returns through the deployment and route map.

narrative.methodEstablished: Validate the complete inventory request before mutation, create permanent events only for accepted operations, and route every browser view through one server-provided canonical application URL.
narrative.result: Milestone 6 was completed and Milestone 7 reached approximately 70–75 percent, producing a safe transaction processor and a stable routed interface rather than disconnected forms and prototypes.
lessonsLearned: Rejected operations should be diagnosable without altering operational history.
Inventory movement must preserve totals while changing source and destination balances.
Reusable views are more maintainable than one page per record.
Embedded navigation requires explicit canonical URLs.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentSummary: Work completed across Milestones 6 and 7 moved the project from a collection of spreadsheet records and experimental pages into a functioning inventory application with validated transactions, permanent event history, live product information, current SDS access, and reusable browser views. Milestone 6 established the processing layer. Accepted inventory requests now update current quantities and create permanent operational events. Invalid requests remain available for diagnosis but cannot change inventory or create false event records. Milestone 7 then connected that data to a routed web application. The current interface includes Home, Inventory, Product Directory, reusable Product Detail, and SDS Directory views. The Product View combines product identity, an image, manufacturer information, inventory by location, and the current SDS record.

sections.title: Embedded Navigation Problem and Solution
sections.contentSummary: The route map worked, but page-to-page navigation became unstable when Apps Script pages were used inside an embedded environment. Problem Relative links such as ?view=inventory depended on the browser resolving the correct frame and base URL. Links could work when opened directly yet fail, disappear, or replace the wrong frame when embedded. Solution The server now provides one shared appUrl to every template. Navigation links use the complete Apps Script web-app URL and send every request back through doGet(e) and the route map. Why the problem occurred In this structure, target="_top" , target="_parent" , and relative paths can refer to different frame levels depending on how the application was opened. Routing and navigation therefore had to be treated as separate systems. sections.title: Verification
sections.contentSummary: Testing covered both successful operating paths and deliberate failure cases. Received inventory increased the correct destination quantity. Used Up and Removed actions reduced the correct source quantity. Moved inventory preserved the total while changing locations. Count Corrected replaced the recorded amount with the verified count. Unknown destinations produced no partial source subtraction. Over-limit removals and moves produced no negative inventory. Rejected requests remained visible for diagnosis but created no operational event. The same Product View displayed different products when only the ID changed. Inventory-by-location displayed the correct matching records. Current SDS records and document links loaded from live sheet data. Shared navigation worked across all existing views. The existing Inventory View continued to function after routing changes.

email.subject: Klinswork Inventory Milestones 6 and 7 Update
email.body: The inventory system can now safely process supplies being received, used, removed, moved, or corrected. Invalid requests are blocked before they can create partial quantity changes or false history. The application also now combines product details, current quantities by location, and SDS documents through stable reusable views. Milestone 6 is complete, and Milestone 7 is approximately 70–75 percent complete.
